label: adult-s9
summary: The model gives the predicted chance of a low income (the lower of the two income classes in the data) as a sigmoid of a score that is mostly linear in the inputs. The direct edges carry most of the ranking: switching them off drops the training AUC from 0.9074 to 0.7083, while switching off the six hidden parts together leaves 0.9021. The largest direct terms lower the predicted chance: capital gain (-3.38 per sd), being a husband (-1.26) and education level (-1.09). The hidden parts add on the score: a capital-gain gate that opens between 4400 US dollars and 4600 US dollars and pushes the score further down for the 2143 training people for whom it is open; a working-hours hinge at 50 hours, below which shorter weeks raise the predicted chance, more steeply for very short weeks; a fixed step up for the 12,914 never-married people; and small category flags fitted to few rows: preschool (64 people, predicted at near certainty), working without pay (17) or born in Iran (50), born in Honduras (14, a large downward offset that runs against their observed low-income rate of 85.7%), unmarried and a professional-school degree.

tool_bugs: (1) No way to delete an evidence record, so accidental duplicates can only be amended. (2) A typed '≈' formula with nested relu in a hypothesis was refused as bare numbers for its inner coefficients (0.977, 0.334, 0.00808, 0.437) while the outer ones passed, so the closed forms were attached as analytical_formula evidence instead of typed in the text. (3) --render has no allow_numbers, so a literal such as '$50,000' cannot appear in the summary. (4) amend_evidence has no allow_numbers either (record numbers in a narrative are refused). (5) query_ablate(direct=true) reports 0 direct edges once the direct edges are routed through an identity node inside a leaf; edge ablations on '->identity_0' were used instead.
